question.text: Which return metric best represents the actual cash returned to AIF investors?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines DPI as the amount paid out to investors, calculated as cumulative distributions divided by paid-in capital. RVPI captures unrealised value, and TVPI includes RVPI, so only DPI measures cash actually returned. The Trap: TVPI and RVPI lean on valuations that may not materialise; Gross IRR ignores fees. DPI is the only listed metric tied to realised cash distributions. Note: Earlier wording branded DPI as a "gold standard" and "money in the bank" metric and told distributors to prioritise it over other track-record metrics. Those evaluative claims are not directly supported by the checked workbook and have been removed; the explanation now stays with the cash-distribution definition and the DPI/RVPI/TVPI relationship.
